position: Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties and Privacy Office; Immigration Detention Ombudsman and CIS Ombudsman
proposal: The Mandate says the Office of the General Counsel should absorb the necessary functions and staff of the Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties and the Privacy Office, under a political deputy general counsel. It also says the Immigration Detention Ombudsman office (which needs a statutory change) and the CIS Ombudsman office (also needing a statutory change) should be eliminated.
remaining: Statutory change to abolish OIDO (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2020, section 106) and the CIS Ombudsman (Homeland Security Act section 452).

status_summary: On or before 2025-03-21 DHS began reductions in force at the Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties (CRCL), the Office of the Immigration Detention Ombudsman (OIDO) and the CIS Ombudsman (CISOMB). Three nonprofits sued on 2025-04-24 (RFK Human Rights v. DHS, D.D.C.), and a DHS declaration of 2025-05-22 said the offices would stay open with much smaller staffs, roughly 20 casework staff for CRCL and 5 to 7 each for the ombudsman offices, against about 140, 100 and 40 staff before. A declaration by the CIS Ombudsman filed on 2026-02-13 reports that CRCL and OIDO had brought back a few former employees and that administrative functions were realigned to the Management Directorate; none of the offices has been folded into the General Counsel or abolished.

timeline.event: Reports said DHS was carrying out reductions in force at CRCL, OIDO and CISOMB.
Three nonprofits sued DHS in the District of Columbia to restore the three offices (RFK Human Rights v. DHS, No. 1:25-cv-01270).
A DHS declaration outlined plans to keep the three offices open with much smaller staffs (CRCL about 20 casework staff plus leadership, each ombudsman 5 to 7), using detailees.
Judge Reyes denied a temporary restraining order without prejudice; the preliminary injunction motion stayed under consideration.

A declaration by the CIS Ombudsman, who was also acting as deputy for CRCL and OIDO, said CRCL and OIDO had rehired a few employees who left in the reduction in force and that human resources, contracting, finance and IT functions were realigned to the Management Directorate.

title: Fold CRCL and Privacy into the General Counsel; end the two DHS ombudsman offices
uncertainties: No ruling on the preliminary injunction motion was found; the Clearinghouse page (updated 2025-08-19) shows no entries after June 2025, and the February 2026 declaration is the latest court filing seen. The staff figures before and after the cuts come from a news summary of the DHS declaration. Court filings were reported to mention FY2026 budget language describing OIDO as eliminated; the February 2026 declaration read in this review does not mention it, and it was not independently checked. Whether the General Counsel absorbed any CRCL or Privacy Office duties was not found, and the Privacy Office was not covered by the sources found.
